title: Additional African country agricultural evidence leads
purpose: Extend the GoOrganicAfrica country evidence programme beyond the first nine West African profiles. These are source leads and carefully qualified national observations, not activated calculator data.
publication_rules: Do not activate a country or commodity profile from aggregate cereal production alone.
Require crop-specific harvested area and production with compatible definitions before accepting a yield.
Keep farm-gate, wholesale and retail prices separate; record market, date, grade, unit and currency.
Do not infer farm input budgets from national price indices or food retail prices.
Do not convert broad cereal aggregates into maize, rice or other individual commodity values.
Do not change calculator formulas or existing ten active country profiles.

cross_country_sources.title: FAOSTAT crop production, yield and harvested area
cross_country_sources.units: harvested area hectares; production tonnes; yield hectograms per hectare
cross_country_sources.quality_note: FAO metadata says source data can originate from official national statistics, surveys, administrative records and estimates based on expert observations. Preserve source lineage and flags; do not treat every value as a direct national survey observation.

cross_country_sources.title: FAO GIEWS Country Briefs
cross_country_sources.quality_note: Useful for current seasonal conditions, aggregate cereal balances, monitored food prices and policy developments. Country briefs do not replace crop-specific national production and farm-budget tables.

next_steps: For Mauritania, visually inspect the Trarza yearbook PDF pages containing rice area and production, then obtain national EMEA annual survey tables and livestock census data.
For Mali, extract CPS/Ministry regional crop tables and reconcile the FAOSTAT 2024 maize, paddy rice and watermelon series against matching harvested area.
For The Gambia, locate the newest Ministry of Agriculture crop survey; do not use the 1988-2012 area-sown series as current harvested-area yields.
For Guinea-Bissau, identify the national agricultural census/survey tables and extract region-level rice and coarse-grain production.
For Chad, obtain crop-specific provincial estimates and market/input prices by Sahelian and Sudanian production systems.
For Central African Republic, prioritize prefecture-level crop assessment and accessible market evidence, explicitly recording conflict and displacement constraints.
For all six countries, collect dated producer prices, input quotations, labour and livestock budgets before creating calculator profiles.
Keep all six countries research-only until their crop-specific evidence is reconciled and independently reviewed.
